lead.headline: Gunman kills 3 children and a teacher at Bend, Oregon, elementary school
lead.dek: A 16-year-old shot through the locked doors of Silver Rail Elementary; a bystander followed and killed him, police said
body: A 16-year-old with a long gun fired his way through the locked doors of Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, shortly before 1 p.m. Thursday and killed three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher before a community member who followed him inside shot him dead, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.

A 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were in critical condition at St. Charles Medical Center, police said. The first 911 call came from a driver who said someone with a long gun had fired on their vehicle; dozens of calls followed reporting a shooter inside the K-5 school of more than 400 students. Officers arrived within three minutes and found him dead.

Police did not name the suspect, a Bend resident, or say whether he had any link to the school; the ATF received trace results on the weapon Thursday evening, NBC News reported. Gov. Tina Kotek said the bystander "heroically intervened to stop further loss of life." Bend-La Pine Schools canceled Friday classes, and a vigil was held at Drake Park.

briefs.headline: FBI probes dozens of powder letters sent to senators, election offices
briefs.summary: Powder letters went to Sens. Schumer, Padilla and Murphy and to election offices in at least 15 states; early tests found it not hazardous, sources said.

briefs.headline: Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution
briefs.summary: Trump wrote that many people "would rather not watch him die"; Nidal Hasan still faces a firing squad Dec. 3. Speaker Johnson had called a stream a recruiting tool.

briefs.headline: Warsh gives no signal on an October hike as Fed quiet period nears
briefs.summary: In Bangkok on Friday the Fed chair said "I don't prejudge meetings." CME odds of an Oct. 28 hike fell to about 30% after topping 50% on Wednesday's CPI.

briefs.headline: Maduro pleads not guilty to torture conspiracy in Manhattan court
briefs.summary: Maduro called the superseding indictment "false accusations"; Judge Alvin Hellerstein moved the trial to June 14, 2027. It alleges nine victims, three Americans.

briefs.headline: Ukraine resumes refinery strikes as Zelenskyy says he feels betrayed
briefs.summary: A Ryazan refinery caught fire hours after Zelenskyy told the Financial Times "The block is out. We're done." Starshield speeds were back by Thursday, Kyiv's envoy said.

briefs.headline: Houthi missiles hit Yemen's presidential palace in Aden, killing 5
briefs.summary: Two of the prime minister's bodyguards were among the dead and 16 were hurt, the health minister said. The coalition said Riyadh's airport was hit 20 times in 11 days.

briefs.headline: China and North Korea open Yalu River bridge 12 years late
briefs.summary: Trucks flying both flags crossed the 3,026-meter, four-lane span between Dandong and Sinuiju Thursday; Premier Li Qiang said ties were "entering a new stage."

briefs.headline: Somalia sets 2027 elections over opposition objections
briefs.summary: The commission set parliamentary votes for April 15 and a presidential vote for May 15, 2027. Ex-president Farmaajo called it a "dangerous threat" to statehood.

briefs.headline: 2 die as vehicle leaves elevated interstate in Charleston
briefs.summary: A vehicle went over the wall just past the eastbound I-64/I-77 split about 5 p.m. Thursday; two of three occupants died, police said. Four men died on the same stretch Aug. 21.

briefs.headline: Diesel leak in Cabin Creek area reaches Kanawha River
briefs.summary: A trucking company's 12,000-gallon tank leaked early Thursday into Slaughters Creek and the river, DEP said. Booms are out; the nearest water intake is 100-plus miles downstream.

briefs.headline: Boone jurors hear 911 call, grandmother's statement
briefs.summary: Jurors heard the 911 call and Donna Stone's recorded statement Thursday; relatives said they had not seen the girl since 2020. Court resumes at 9 a.m. Friday.

briefs.headline: Man charged with murder in 2016 Dolly Sods killing
briefs.summary: Richard Nichols, arrested in Indiana, is held without bond in the death of Ivan Perlis, whose remains a hunter found in November 2016 with three gunshot wounds, MetroNews reported.

regional.item: Mason County's November school levy also decides whether $90M in data center taxes reach the schools, the state treasurer said Thursday.
South Charleston's police chief announced his retirement at Thursday's council meeting after more than 19 years leading the department.
Parkersburg opens its nearly $15M, 46,000-square-foot Simms Powell Pavilion in City Park Monday with a 4 p.m. ribbon cutting.

away.item: Shaftsbury says North Bennington's Jan. 7 water-rate vote broke the Open Meeting Law; village trustees took the dispute up Tuesday.

hotspots.item: The Webster County Commission is back to first- and third-Wednesday 9 a.m. meetings after four months of monthly sessions, it confirmed Oct. 7, the Echo said.
A state hearing on Novant's proposed $15M freestanding ER in Hampstead was set for 11 a.m. today at the Pender County library, WECT reported Sept. 3.

briefs.headline: Prince George advance vote hits one-day record of 1,592
briefs.summary: Wednesday's turnout lifted the three-day advance total to 3,817 ballots, 5.9% of 64,314 eligible voters. General voting is Saturday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.

briefs.headline: Four councillors demand closed meeting with Yu over leak
briefs.summary: Scott, Ramsay, Bennett and Polillo say Mayor Simon Yu disclosed a confidential whistleblower complaint. Yu said he paid almost $26,000 for his own probe and acted properly.

briefs.headline: Eby pledges $250M Surrey transit; Conservatives pitch bridge
briefs.summary: Eby promised Surrey-White Rock bus rapid transit with Ottawa; the Conservatives vowed to scrap the $8B Massey Tunnel for a 10-lane bridge and dropped a candidate over Hitler posts.

briefs.headline: NDP defends Crown land compensation plan after leaked report
briefs.summary: Northern Beat reported cabinet weighed new compensation rules for forestry tenures on about 400 Crown parcels going to First Nations. Eby said cabinet approved only engagement.

briefs.headline: Carney tells Calgary rally turnout will decide referendum
briefs.summary: The prime minister urged a vote to stay and a no on the nine other questions; the PMO put the crowd at 5,000. Alberta votes Monday. Carney is in Edmonton Friday.

briefs.headline: Ottawa puts $100M into Nova Scotia offshore wind surveys
briefs.summary: Energy Minister Tim Hodgson announced the money in Dartmouth for wind, ocean and seafloor data for the Wind West project. Nova Scotia aims to license 5 gigawatts by 2030.

briefs.headline: Artemis II heat shield had 9 char-loss spots, down from 103
briefs.summary: NASA's post-flight analysis found cracking and char loss fell about tenfold from Artemis I after a shortened reentry path. Orion splashed down 0.59 miles from target April 10.

briefs.headline: RIKEN silicon qubits hold 99.99% fidelity three at a time
briefs.summary: A five-qubit spin array driven through one microwave line kept gate fidelity above 99.99% with three qubits running at once and about 99.9% with all five, per Nature Physics.

briefs.headline: Genome study traces Native Hawaiians through Easter Island
briefs.summary: Stanford and UC San Diego researchers analyzed more than 1,000 Polynesian genomes in Science and found Rapa Nui, 7,000 km away, is Hawaii's closest genetic relative.

briefs.headline: IUCN update lists 44% of reef-building corals as threatened
briefs.summary: The first full Red List reassessment since 2008 classed 340 of 774 assessable species as vulnerable or worse. Its data stop at 2020, before the 2023-25 bleaching event.

briefs.headline: GPT-6-Astra solves 49 of 50 physics problems in new test
briefs.summary: A 35-researcher team coordinated by Suvrat Raju built TheoPhysEval from unpublished problems. OpenAI's model scored 98% at under $3 each, Anthropic's Opus 5.5 92%, Gemini 3.8 Flash 68%.

briefs.headline: Anthropic gives METR six researchers employee-level access
briefs.summary: The nonprofit's team gets laptops, office space and internal tools and may publish without Anthropic's approval, the company said. Redactions are limited to three categories.

briefs.headline: Scan finds 30 websites planting prompt injections in headers
briefs.summary: Signals Corps searched 217 million Common Crawl responses and found about 8,000 sites sending header messages to AI agents. It judged 22 of the 30 injection attempts pranks.

weather_ear: Friday's forecast, from Jim Claudtore, follows at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers-New River carry no regional line today; the Williams River's recession from Thursday's crest is read in Sports & Sportsman.
